About the job

Founded in 2018 with co-headquarters in Dublin and Boston, Tines powers some of the world's most important workflows. Our intelligent workflow platform applies AI, automation, and integration with human ingenuity to drive real business results.

Tines serves a diverse range of customers, from startups to public companies, including Canva, Databricks, Elastic, Kayak, Intercom, and McKesson. As an integrator across the entire tech stack, Tines is vendor-agnostic integrating with any API-enabled service. This flexibility enables our customers to achieve their highest-priority goals faster. And because Tines is secure and private by design, it’s popular with security, IT, engineering, finance, and other security-focused teams.

At Tines, we're driven by our values of Simplicity, Speed, and Soundness. We're committed to delivering exceptional customer experiences while fostering a company culture that nurtures individual curiosity, growth, and integrity. We’re excited about what’s next, and we’re looking for others to join us on our journey.


This is a remote position that must be based in the Pacific time zone.*



The Role

We're hiring a Deal Desk Analyst reporting into our Revenue Operations organization. This role is the engine of Tines' day to day deal operations. You will turn quotes, order forms, and approvals around quickly and accurately, and act as first line support for our Sales reps, CSMs, and RMs, keeping deals moving and the field unblocked.

You will work with high level direction and own a clearly defined scope, escalating genuinely complex or non standard deals to senior members of the team. It's an ideal role for someone who thrives on responsiveness, accuracy, and high transaction volume, and who wants to build deep quote to cash expertise as Tines modernizes its tooling.

Our ideal candidate is highly detail oriented, numerically literate, and very comfortable with spreadsheets. They are organized and diligent, and an excellent communicator — both verbally and in writing — as you'll be working with a wide array of teams and levels of seniority. Finally, this is a start up, so ideally you're excited by the prospect of building something from the ground up alongside others who are equally energized by the opportunity.

What You Will Be Doing


Process deals. Create and manage quotes, order forms, and amendments in CPQ accurately and within SLA.
Route approvals. Drive deals through the approval matrix, tracking status and looping in the right approvers to keep cycle times low.
Support reps. Be the first point of contact for day to day pricing, packaging, and process questions, responding with a service mindset and advising on alternate contract options to drive deal closure.
Protect data quality. Maintain deal hygiene and accurate opportunity and quote data in Salesforce.
Support the close. Help manage order processing and prioritize effectively during periods of high volume, with schedule flexibility at month and quarter end.
Escalate well. Identify complex or non standard deals early and hand them off cleanly to the senior deal desk.
Partner cross-functionally. Partner with Legal, Finance, and Sales to facilitate, process, and execute standard and non-standard deals.
Improve tooling. Help support and improve our CPQ tool, DealHub, and the associated workflows.



What You Bring With You 


3–4 years in deal desk, sales operations, or order management within B2B SaaS.
Familiarity with CPQ and quote to cash processes (Salesforce, DealHub, or similar).
Detail oriented, organized, and responsive; comfortable with high transaction volume and period end pressure.
Strong stakeholder service mindset and clear, well structured communication.
Understanding of SaaS business models, subscription based pricing, and revenue recognition principles.
Not fazed by ambiguity or uncertainty, and comfortable working in a dynamic, hyper growth environment.
A clear and thoughtful communicator when discussing and sharing sensitive data with a range of business functions.
Strong MS Excel/Google Sheets skills (required).

Target Annual Compensation: Up to $140,000 OTE, comprised of a competitive base salary, target bonus, and equity.

Applicants for this opportunity must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time.

At Tines, we’re all about trying new things and taking the leap. If you’re second-guessing your application, we hope you’ll trust your gut and take the leap too! Applying for a new job isn’t always easy, especially if you’re thinking of a career pivot – but we’re big believers in learning and growth here at Tines, so you’ve nothing to worry about. A variety of experience, perspectives, and voices makes us the company we are. We’d love to hear from you.

About the job

Job Title: Product Lead

Description & Requirements:

 

KORE1, a nationwide provider of staffing and recruiting solutions, has an immediate opening for Product Lead in Fort Lauderdale, FL.

 

THIS ROLE IS ONSITE IN FORT LAUDERDALE, FL.

 

Product Lead, Bond OS




Build the operating system for patient-centered care

Bond OS is the platform layer for modern care delivery. It brings together structured patient intake, longitudinal patient context, provider review, clinic and administrative operations, orders, prescriptions, commerce, platform APIs, analytics, support workflows, and applied AI/ML within one connected system.
Healthcare delivery is often fragmented: intake happens in one place, clinical review in another, order and prescription updates somewhere else, operations in spreadsheets, support in tickets, and analytics after the fact. Bond OS brings these workflows together through unified patient context, clear processes for every role, durable platform foundations, and intelligent assistance that improves speed, quality, and safety.
We are hiring a Product Lead to own the Bond OS roadmap across both product experiences and platform capabilities. This is a senior, hands-on leadership role for someone who can move comfortably between client conversations, patient and provider workflows, technical contracts, data models, operational edge cases, AI/ML release standards, and close collaboration with engineering and design.

Why This Role Matters

Bond OS is entering its next chapter. The core platform is live, the product surface is expanding, and the opportunity is to make the system more connected, patient-centered, operationally powerful, and intelligent.
This role will shape how the platform scales: how intake becomes useful clinical context, how providers and clinic teams manage their work, how orders and prescriptions are tracked, how clients understand performance, how APIs and permissions become stronger platform capabilities, and how applied AI/ML is responsibly introduced into high-consequence workflows.
The mandate is clear: turn a powerful care-delivery platform into a sharper, more unified operating system.

What You Will Lead

Bond OS Roadmap

Own the product roadmap across the full platform, including:
Patient intake, patient portal, and longitudinal patient context
Provider workflows, review queues, clinical decision-making, and safety review
Clinic and administrative operations, group management, permissions, and oversight
Orders, prescriptions, catalog, commerce, payments, promotions, and fulfillment handoffs
Platform APIs, integrations, auditability, data contracts, and status models
Analytics for operations, outcomes, quality, and performance
Applied AI/ML across intake, summarization, triage, drafting, operations, and decision-support context

You will establish priorities, make tradeoffs, sequence dependencies, and ensure the roadmap remains grounded in client value, patient impact, operational leverage, and engineering realities.

Platform Foundations

Define and protect the core building blocks of Bond OS, including patients, intake, encounters, decisions, orders, prescriptions, catalog items, groups, roles, permissions, audit events, statuses, and AI artifacts.
Strong product leadership will make the platform simpler and more durable by turning repeated workflows into shared systems, edge cases into clearly defined states, and client-specific requests into reusable capabilities.

Client and User Discovery

Partner directly with clients, providers, clinic and administrative teams, operators, support, design, engineering, and leadership. You will observe real workflows, identify where care delivery breaks down, and translate those insights into meaningful product decisions.
Discovery should directly influence the roadmap. The goal is not simply to collect opinions, but to understand where Bond OS can create measurable value for patients, providers, clients, and internal teams.

Applied AI/ML Product Direction

AI/ML is a core part of the Bond OS product strategy. Early opportunities include assisted intake summarization, missing-data detection, suggested triage priority, provider-facing drafting, operational intelligence, quality analytics, and decision-support context.
You will determine which use cases are worth pursuing, define what successful output looks like, establish how model-backed features are evaluated before launch, and determine how humans review or override results. You will also define how failures are handled and how performance is monitored after release.
Our standard is practical and rigorous: AI-supported features must be assistive, evaluated, observable, auditable, human-supervised, and suppressible when safety or confidence requirements are not met.

Product Execution and Specification Quality

Write clear product specifications that engineering and design can confidently execute. Strong specifications should include:
User goals and role-specific workflows
System states and API contracts
Validation behavior and data requirements
Audit and logging requirements
Internationalization requirements
Acceptance criteria
Rollout plans and release standards

For AI/ML-powered features, specifications should also define model inputs and outputs, evaluation criteria, red-team scenarios, confidence and fallback behavior, human-review experiences, monitoring requirements, and go/no-go thresholds.

Product Operating Cadence

Maintain the product source of truth, including what is live, in progress, blocked, removed, dependent on other work, and considered complete.

Establish a clear written cadence that provides leadership, clients, and internal teams with visibility into decisions, tradeoffs, risks, dependencies, and progress.




What You Will Do

Build and maintain the Bond OS roadmap across patient, provider, clinic, administrative, order, prescription, commerce, API, analytics, operations, and AI/ML experiences.
Translate client, user, clinical, operational, and technical insights into clear product direction.
Partner with engineering on API contracts, schemas, state machines, validation behavior, performance, reliability, and integration boundaries.
Partner with design to create thoughtful workflows that reduce cognitive load and make complex care operations easier to navigate.
Prioritize the smallest valuable releases that strengthen the platform without creating long-term product debt.
Lead applied AI/ML product discovery and develop the first comprehensive AI/ML product requirements for Bond OS.
Define release standards for high-consequence workflows, including safety, auditability, permissions, internationalization, test coverage, and operational fallbacks.
Communicate roadmap priorities and tradeoffs to internal stakeholders and, when appropriate, strategic clients.
Establish the product discipline needed for a small, senior team to move quickly while maintaining a high standard of quality.




The Person Who Will Thrive Here

You are a systems thinker with strong product judgment. You reason from first principles, communicate clearly, and turn ambiguity into a practical sequence of work. You are comfortable working deeply within workflows, APIs, data models, permissions, state machines, and edge cases.
You care about product quality because clarity creates operational leverage in healthcare software. Strong hierarchy, understandable states, thoughtful defaults, precise language, and reliable fallback processes matter. The best product decisions make the system easier to understand for patients, providers, operators, clients, and engineers.
You are also practical. You can maintain a broad platform vision while delivering small, high-quality releases. You know how to say yes through thoughtful sequencing and how to say no by clearly explaining tradeoffs. You are excited to work with a lean team while building something ambitious.




Experience We Value

We care most about judgment, product taste, execution, and technical credibility. Strong candidates may bring a combination of the following:
Six or more years of product management or product leadership experience, ideally owning complex software from strategy through launch
Experience building platforms, SaaS products, healthcare technology, fintech, logistics, marketplaces, developer platforms, operational systems, commerce products, or other high-consequence software
Experience in healthcare, health technology, telehealth, pharmacy, electronic prescribing, care operations, or regulated data
Experience working directly with customers or strategic clients and translating their needs into scalable product capabilities
Technical fluency with API contracts, schemas, state machines, data models, permissions, validation, integrations, observability, and engineering tradeoffs
Strong written communication skills across product requirements, specifications, roadmap memos, technical decision documents, launch plans, and executive updates
Experience developing AI/ML products, particularly around evaluation, guardrails, human-in-the-loop experiences, model observability, red-teaming, drift monitoring, and responsible release processes
Familiarity with healthcare data standards such as FHIR, SDC, HL7, or LOINC
Experience working within a small or fast-moving team where sound product judgment mattered more than heavy process
A background in engineering, design, data, operations, clinical workflows, or technical product management




Compensation depends on experience but is typically $120K-$200K.

The Technical Product Owner (TPO) is the tactical owner of a team’s backlog and capacity. While the Technical Product Manager (TPM) sets strategic direction at the capability level, the TPO ensures the team delivers the highest-value work in alignment with capability priorities. Acting as the single-threaded owner of the team backlog, the TPO bridges business, technology, and delivery execution, consolidating responsibilities traditionally split between a Product Owner and Scrum Master.

About the job

Why We Exist

Your car and your home are your most important assets, yet the experience of owning them is stuck in the 90s. Every part of the journey - insurance, repairs, financing, maintenance - is fragmented, complicated, and expensive. Jerry.ai is building the first app to manage it all.

We started with car insurance in 2019, became one of the top three brokers in the country, then added driving insights, diagnostics, and a repair marketplace. We've reached 5M+ customers, raised $240M+, scaled revenue 70X, and became profitable in early 2024.

Why We’re Hiring This Role

We are fundamentally changing the way people think about and shop for insurance. And the opportunity is massive: car insurance alone is a $300B market in the U.S. We spent the last few years building our supply (we work with 100+ insurance carriers) and our technical infrastructure (60% of policies today are sold automatically without human intervention, 90% of inbound customer inquiries are resolved via AI and automation). The next chapter is about accelerating our growth – going from 5M to 50M customers and becoming a $10B business by 2030.

The Growth team owns the entire customer sign-up and purchase funnel for our car insurance marketplace (our core product today), and drives how millions of people discover, evaluate, and become a Jerry customer.

Our funnel is healthy (we're profitable at 5M customers), but our product is becoming increasingly complex as we onboard new insurance carriers and expand beyond car insurance. As a result, our Growth team is expanding, and we need a Product Manager who can take on product walkthroughs, user feedback synthesis, new feature builds, product launches, and funnel improvements as we continue growing.

Why You Will (Or Won't) Like Working Here


Direct exposure: You'll report directly to our VP of Growth with visibility to the c-suite team. You'll have visibility into product strategy, business model tradeoffs, and roadmap decisions from Day One.
Time zone constraint: The engineering team is partly based in China. You'll need to maintain 3–4 hours of daily overlap with China business hours. This is a real constraint on your schedule, and it's non-negotiable.
Small team: The Growth team has 3 Product Managers (including you) and the surface area is huge, which means you'll have to be scrappy, but also that you'll have lots of scope and ownership.
Fast shipping culture: We run weekly sprints. Products that take 6-12 months to ship elsewhere, we launch in 1-2 months. This means faster learning and faster growth, but also a more demanding environment.


What You'll Own


Phase 1: In your first few months, your job is to learn how to be a product manager and develop a deep, ground-level understanding of how our funnels perform. You'll conduct structured product walkthroughs to map user journeys and identify friction points. You'll own user feedback monitoring: pulling signals from reviews, support tickets, and research and turning them into actionable insight.
